text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Financial mismanagement and unimaginative policies of the Zimbabwe Football Association have been identified as the key factors plaguing Zimbabwean soccer for the past five years.
- Zimbabwe's external debt is projected to reach Z$60.95 billion ($5.4 billion) by the end of 1998.
- A row between the finance ministry and the Post and Telecommunications Corporation threatens the implementation of the country's first cellular telephone network.

- The United States Congressional Black Caucus says it will back Zimbabwe's fight to have the ban on ivory trade lifted at next month's conference of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species conference in Harare.
- The Organisation of African Unity Council of Ministers has recommended that existing regional economic blocs become the legal building structures of the proposed Africa Economic Community.

- Zimbabwe's Comptroller and Auditor-General will investigate the alleged abuse of the War Veterans Compensation Fund in which the state is said to have lost millions of dollars to undeserving individuals.
